t.1.199.1: Drupada said: It is just as you have told me today, O Vidura of great wisdom; I too feel the highest joy now that this alliance has been made, O lord.
t.1.199.2: A journey to the home of these great-souled ones would indeed be fitting; but it is not fitting for me to say this myself in words.
t.1.199.4: And let Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, who know dharma, come, and then let the Pāṇḍavas go; for these two tigers among men are devoted to what is dear and beneficial to them.
t.1.199.3: But when the heroic son of Kuntī, Yudhiṣṭhira, deems it fit, and likewise Bhīmasena and Arjuna, and the twins, those bulls among men, …
t.1.199.6: Then Vāsudeva said, "The going pleases me, or else let it be as King Drupada, the knower of all dharma, thinks fit."
t.1.199.5: O king, we, together with our followers, are wholly dependent upon you in everything. Whatever you tell us out of affection, that we shall do.
t.1.199.7: Just as the heroic, mighty-armed Dāśārha, the best of men, considers to be fitting for the time, that very resolve is settled in my mind as well.
t.1.199.8: For just as the illustrious sons of Kuntī are now mine, so too, without doubt, are the sons of Pāṇḍu Vāsudeva's.
t.1.199.10: Then they, having been granted leave by the great-souled Drupada, the Pāṇḍavas, Kṛṣṇa, and Vidura of great wisdom,
t.1.199.9: Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī and son of Dharma, does not contemplate the welfare of these men as much as Keśava, that tiger among men, contemplates it.
t.1.199.12: And Dhṛtarāṣṭra the Kaurava, too, having heard that the heroes had arrived, sent the Kauravas forth to receive the Pāṇḍavas.
t.1.199.11: Taking Draupadī Kṛṣṇā and the illustrious Kuntī with them, they went happily, enjoying themselves along the way, to the city named after the elephant.
t.1.199.14: Surrounded by them, those heroes, the great chariot-warriors, shining in splendour, then slowly entered the city of Hāstinapura.
t.1.199.13: And Vikarṇa the great archer, and Citrasena, O Bhārata, and Droṇa the supreme archer, and Kṛpa Gautama as well.
t.1.199.15: The city, where those tigers among men, the destroyers of sorrow and grief, were present, seemed as if bursting with excitement.
t.1.199.16: Then the Pāṇḍavas heard many and varied pleasing words, uttered by those who wished to do them a kindness, words that went straight to the heart.
t.1.199.17: Here once more comes that tiger among men, the knower of dharma, who protects us righteously as though we were his own heirs.
t.1.199.19: Has not the greatest joy for all of us been accomplished this very day, in that the heroic sons of Kuntī, our protectors, have returned once more?
t.1.199.18: Today it is as if the great king Pāṇḍu, lover of the forest, has come back from the forest, wishing to do what is dear to us; of this there is no doubt.
t.1.199.20: If there is any merit in what we have given, if in what we have offered in sacrifice, if in our austerity, then by that may the Pāṇḍavas dwell in the city for a hundred autumns.
t.1.199.21: Then they paid homage at the feet of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and of the great-souled Bhīṣma, and of the others who were worthy of such honor.
t.1.199.22: After exchanging inquiries about one another's welfare with the whole city, they entered the dwellings by the command of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
t.1.199.23: Those great-souled ones of mighty strength rested for some time, and then they were summoned by King Dhṛtarāṣṭra and by Śāṃtanava.
t.1.199.25: No one will be able to harass you while you dwell there, protected by Pārtha as the thirty gods are by the wielder of the thunderbolt. Having received half of the kingdom, go and settle in Khāṇḍavaprastha.
t.1.199.24: O Kaunteya, together with your brothers, hear this word of mine: let there be no further strife among you; go and settle in Khāṇḍavaprastha.
t.1.199.26: Accepting those words and bowing to the king, all those bulls among men then set out for that dreadful forest. Having obtained half the kingdom, they entered Khāṇḍavaprastha.
t.1.199.27: Then the Pāṇḍavas, having gone there with Kṛṣṇa at their head, those unfallen ones adorned that city like heaven.
t.1.199.28: Then, in a holy and auspicious region, the great chariot-warriors, led by Dvaipāyana, performed a rite of propitiation and had a city measured out.
t.1.199.29: It was adorned with moats that resembled the ocean, and furnished with a rampart that stood enveloping the very sky.
t.1.199.30: With its wall gleaming like pale white clouds and resembling a heap of snow, that finest of cities shone as Bhogavatī shines with its Nāgas.
t.1.199.31: It was guarded by gates of fearsome aspect that looked like Garuḍa with his two wings spread, and by gate-towers that looked like banks of clouds and rivalled Mount Mandara.
t.1.199.33: Adorned with sharp hooks and śataghnīs and with arrays of war-engines, and with great wheels of iron, that finest of cities shone splendidly.
t.1.199.35: That Indraprastha, resembling Triviṣṭapa, shone forth like a massed bank of clouds swelling in the sky, wreathed all about with lightning.
t.1.199.32: Fitted with many kinds of piercing, well-protected works equipped with weapons, and ringed with spears like two-tongued serpents, furnished with towers for practice and guarded by warriors, that city shone brightly.
t.1.199.34: With its great highways well laid out and free from any harassment by the deities, the city shone with splendid white mansions of many kinds.
t.1.199.36: There, in that charming and auspicious place, the residence of the Kauravya shone forth, filled with wealth, like the abode of the Lord of Wealth.
t.1.199.37: There came, O king, twice-born men, the best among the knowers of all the Vedas, and likewise those versed in all languages, and they chose to make their dwelling there.
t.1.199.38: Merchants seeking wealth came there to that land from every direction, and then men skilled in all the crafts also arrived there to settle.
t.1.199.39: And all around the city there were delightful gardens, with mango trees, hog-plum trees, nīpa trees, aśoka trees, and campaka trees as well.
t.1.199.40: It was adorned with puṃnāga and nāgapuṣpa trees, with lakucas and jackfruit trees, with śālas, palmyras and kadambas, and with bakulas together with ketakas.
t.1.199.41: It was adorned with charming trees in full bloom, bent low under the weight of their fruit, with prācīnāmalakas, lodhras, and richly flowering aṅkolas.
t.1.199.43: With trees ever laden with flowers and fruit, it was thronged with flocks of many kinds of birds, and it resounded with the cries of maddened peacocks and of cuckoos forever in rapture.
t.1.199.42: It was graced with rose-apple and pāṭalā trees, with kubjakas and atimuktakas, with oleanders and pārijātas, and with many other kinds of trees.
t.1.199.45: And with exceedingly delightful lakes, fragrant with lotuses and water lilies, filled with swans and kāraṇḍava ducks, and adorned with cakravāka birds.
t.1.199.46: There were lovely lotus ponds of many kinds, surrounded by groves, and charming reservoirs, both broad and great.
t.1.199.44: It was adorned with houses as spotless as mirrors, with various bowers of creepers, with charming picture-halls, and likewise with artificial hills, and with ponds of many kinds filled with the finest water.
t.1.199.47: As those Pāṇḍavas dwelt in that great kingdom filled with virtuous people, O great king, their joy grew ever greater.
t.1.199.48: There, once Bhīṣma and the king had settled the matter in accordance with dharma, the Pāṇḍavas became dwellers of Khāṇḍavaprastha.
t.1.199.49: Endowed with those five great archers, each like Indra, that finest of cities shone as Bhogavatī shines with the Nāgas.
t.1.199.50: Having settled them there, the hero Keśava, together with Rāma, then went to Dvāravatī, O king, with the consent of the Pāṇḍavas.
